mainTopic: The minimum amounts of food and of liquids for carrying out on שבת, and which parts count toward them
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the previous discussion, about items that combine because a merchant shows them together as a sample. A new משנה then teaches that carrying out food the size of a dried fig (גרוגרת) on שבת makes one חייב, and all foods combine toward that amount. Shells, seeds, stems, and bran do not count, but רבי יהודה says lentil shells do count because they are cooked and eaten with the lentils. The גמרא asks why bran counts for חלה, and אביי answers that a poor person eats bread with bran, while for שבת the food must be fit for everyone. It then reconciles a ברייתא that has רבי יהודה counting bean shells too: new bean shells count, but old ones do not, because, as רבי אבהו says, they look like flies in the dish. The chapter כלל גדול ends, and a new פרק opens with a משנה listing how much of each liquid makes one liable for carrying it, while רבי שמעון says every liquid is a רביעית. The גמרא explains that the wine amount is enough for a כוס של ברכה, and רב נחמן says that this is a quarter of a רביעית of wine that becomes a רביעית after mixing. רבא begins to bring support for this, and his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing line of the previous discussion: suited for a sample
steps.stepSummary: The previous סוגיא ends by saying that these items combine because a merchant would show them together as one sample.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is suitable for a sample.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the discussion earlier. It explains why certain substances combine for carrying on שבת: a merchant would display them together as one sample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things that are naturally shown or used together count as one unit for the minimum amount. Since a seller piles these items together in his sample, carrying them out on שבת adds up as one amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same logic applies here
It is suitable / fit
A sample that a merchant shows to buyers

phrases.english: Here too, it is suitable for a sample.
phrases.notes: Ends the previous סוגיא. A merchant shows these items together, so they combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the discussion carried over earlier.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Items that are suited to be displayed together as one sample combine toward the amount for carrying on שבת.

steps.title: The משנה: a dried-fig amount of food, and what is not counted
steps.stepSummary: Carrying out a גרוגרת of food makes one חייב. All foods combine, but shells, seeds, stems, and bran are not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who carries out foods the size of a dried fig is liable. The foods combine with each other because they have the same measure. Their shells, seeds, stems, bran, and coarse bran are not counted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the minimum amount of food for being חייב for carrying on שבת and lists the parts that do not count toward that amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because every food has the same measure (a גרוגרת), you may add different foods together, such as half a fig's worth of bread and half of cheese. The inedible parts are left out of the count, because only real food counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A dried fig; the size used to measure food for carrying on שבת
They combine / join together toward the amount
Shell / seed or pit / stem
Bran and coarse bran, the husk parts of grain

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for food in הוצאה on שבת. The rest of this passage tests what counts as part of the food.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who carries out foods
phrases.notes: Carrying from one domain to another on שבת.

phrases.english: the size of a dried fig is liable,
and they combine with one another
because they are equal in their measures.
phrases.notes: All foods share the same measure, so they can be added together.

phrases.english: except for their shells and their seeds,
and their stems, and their bran, and their coarse bran.
phrases.notes: These are not counted toward the amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גרוגרת of food makes one חייב. All foods combine, but shells, seeds, stems, and bran are excluded from the count.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: lentil shells do count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that lentil shells count toward the amount because they are cooked and eaten with the lentils.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: except for lentil shells, which are cooked together with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds an exception to the list of shells that do not count. Lentil shells do count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is that people cook and eat lentils with their shells. So those shells are treated as part of the food, not as waste.

keyTerms.meaning: Lentils
They are cooked together with them

steps.confusionAlert: The word חוּץ ("except") works in opposite directions here. In the first part of the משנה, חוץ means "these are left out of the count." In רבי יהודה's statement, חוץ means "except for lentil shells," so lentil shells are an exception to the exclusion and DO count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
except for the shells of lentils,
which are cooked with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: חוּץ מִקְּלִיפֵּי עֲדָשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees in part with the first opinion's rule about shells.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lentil shells count toward the גרוגרת because they are cooked and eaten with the lentils.

steps.title: Challenge: bran counts for חלה, so why not here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה from the laws of חלה, where bran is counted together with the flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do bran and coarse bran really not combine? But we learned: five quarters of a לוג of flour and a bit more is obligated in חלה, counting the flour, its bran, and its coarse bran!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the rule that bran does not count. It quotes a משנה about חלה where bran is counted toward the amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חלה, the minimum amount of dough includes the bran. That seems to show bran is part of the food. So why does our משנה leave bran out for carrying on שבת?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The portion of dough given to a כהן
Five quarters of a לוג, the minimum flour for חלה

phrases.english: GEMARA: And do bran and coarse bran not combine?
But didn't we learn:
five quarters of a log of flour and a bit more
are obligated in challah,
they and their bran and their coarse bran!
phrases.notes: The bran is counted in the amount for חלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's exclusion of bran.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that bran does not combine toward the amount for carrying on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה counts bran together with flour for חלה, which suggests bran is part of the food.

steps.title: אביי: a poor man eats bread with bran
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that bran counts for חלה because poor people eat bread made from dough with bran. For שבת, the food must be fit for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: because a poor man eats his bread from dough mixed with bran.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. Bran counts for bread and חלה because some people really do eat bread with bran in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread with bran is real food for a poor person, so for חלה the bran is part of the dough. Carrying on שבת is different, because there the food counted must be fit for all people. So bran is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person
Dough mixed with bran (not sifted)

steps.whatToRemember: The same item can count for one law (חלה, where bread eaten by the poor is enough) and not for another (שבת, where the food must be fit for everyone).

phrases.english: Abaye said:
because a poor man eats his bread
made from dough mixed with bran.
phrases.notes: So for bread and חלה, bran is part of the food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שֶׁכֵּן עָנִי אוֹכֵל פִּתּוֹ בְּעִיסָּה בְּלוּסָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between two areas of law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If bran counts for חלה, it should count for שבת too.
steps.terutzMaskana: For חלה, bran counts because poor people eat bread with bran. For שבת, the food must be fit for everyone, so bran is left out.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא says רבי יהודה counts bean shells too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה mentions only lentil shells, but a ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה as counting both bean and lentil shells.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: except for lentil shells, which are cooked with them. Does that mean lentils yes, but beans no? But it was taught: רבי יהודה says: except for the shells of beans and lentils!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's words from the משנה and points out a contradiction with a ברייתא that also includes bean shells.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists only lentils, which suggests bean shells do not count. The ברייתא quotes the same רבי יהודה as counting bean shells too. So the two sources seem to give two different versions of his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Beans
Yes / no

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה it is about to discuss.

phrases.english: except for lentil shells, which are cooked with them.
Lentils yes, beans no?
But it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
except for the shells of beans and lentils!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge, this time about רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that, according to רבי יהודה, bean shells do not count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה as explicitly counting bean shells, which contradicts what the משנה implies.

steps.title: Answer: new beans versus old beans
steps.stepSummary: Both sources are correct. The ברייתא is about new beans, whose shells count. The משנה is about old beans, whose shells do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this is with new ones, that is with old ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources describe different kinds of beans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh, new beans are eaten with their shells, so their shells count (the ברייתא). Old beans' shells are not eaten, so they do not count (the משנה's silence about beans).

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces a resolution)
New / fresh ones
Old ones

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is with new ones, that is with old ones.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is about new beans (shells count). The משנה is about old beans (shells do not count).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּחַדְתֵי, הָא בְּעַתִּיקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא give conflicting versions of רבי יהודה's view on bean shells.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shells of new beans count. Shells of old beans do not.

steps.title: Why don't old bean shells count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason old bean shells do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Old ones — what is the reason they do not count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the answer it just gave. This sets up רבי אבהו's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old beans are still cooked with their shells, so why should their shells be any different from those of new beans? The גמרא wants the logic behind the distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: Old ones, what is the reason they do not count?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the previous step's distinction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the shells of old beans are not counted with the beans.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: they look like flies in the dish
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that old bean shells look like flies in the dish, so people throw them away instead of eating them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: because they look like flies in the bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question. Old bean shells look disgusting, like flies, so nobody eats them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something counts as food only if people actually eat it. New bean shells are eaten with the beans. Old bean shells look like flies, so people throw them out, and they do not count toward the גרוגרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Flies
A bowl / dish

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a shell counts toward the amount depends on whether people actually eat it. Lentil shells and new bean shells count. Bran (for שבת) and old bean shells do not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
because they look like flies in the bowl.
phrases.notes: People find them disgusting and throw them away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאִין כִּזְבוּבִין בַּקְּעָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Old bean shells look like flies in the dish, so people discard them, and they are not treated as food.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק כלל גדול
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula that ends the seventh פרק of מסכת שבת, כלל גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'כלל גדול' (the chapter called 'A Great Principle').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks the end of the chapter called כלל גדול. Nothing new is being argued here. It is a closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every פרק ends with הדרן עלך, a promise that we will come back and learn this chapter again. The discussion of shells and bran from the previous steps is now finished. A brand-new topic starts next.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the formula said when finishing a chapter.
'A Great Principle', the name of the chapter that is ending.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'A Great Principle'
phrases.notes: This is the traditional line said when finishing a perek.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose final discussion ended with רבי אבהו's explanation in step 9.

steps.title: The משנה lists the carrying amounts for each liquid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the minimum amount of each liquid that makes someone liable for carrying it out on שבת. Wine is measured by a cup's dilution, milk by a gulp, honey by enough for a sore, oil by enough for a small limb, and water by enough to wet an eye-salve. All other liquids and waste water are measured by a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who carries out wine is liable for enough to mix a cup. Milk: enough for a gulp. Honey: enough to put on a sore. Oil: enough to smear a small limb. Water: enough to dissolve an eye-salve. All other liquids: a רביעית. All waste water: a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It tells us how much of each liquid a person must carry on שבת to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each liquid gets its own amount based on its smallest normal use. You only become liable for carrying something that is useful. A gulp of milk, a dab of honey, or a smear of oil are each worth something. Liquids with no special small use fall back to the standard amount of a רביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries out (from one domain to another on שבת).
Mixing a cup. Strong wine was diluted with water before drinking.
A gulp or swallow.
A sore or wound caused by rubbing.
An eye-salve, which was dissolved in water before use.
A quarter of a לוג, the standard measure for liquids.

steps.confusionAlert: The amount for wine is NOT a full cup. It is the amount of strong wine that, once mixed with water, makes a proper cup. The גמרא explains exactly how much that is.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who carries out wine —
enough to mix a cup.
phrases.notes: The amount of strong wine that is used, with water, to make a cup.

phrases.english: Milk — enough for a gulp.
Honey — enough to put on a sore.
Oil — enough to smear a small limb.

phrases.aramaic: מַיִם — כְּדֵי לָשׁוּף בָּהֶם אֶת הַקִּילוֹר.
phrases.english: Water — enough to dissolve the eye-salve with it.
And all other liquids — a quarter-log,
and all waste water — a quarter-log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The amount that makes one liable for carrying a liquid depends on that liquid's smallest normal use. Liquids without a special use are measured by a רביעית.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says every liquid is measured by a quarter-log
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that all liquids are measured by a רביעית. In his view, the smaller amounts apply only to someone who stores such small quantities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: all of them are measured by a רביעית. All these smaller amounts were said only about people who store them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He gives one amount, a רביעית, for every liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a normal person, tiny amounts like a gulp or a dab are not worth carrying, so the amount is a רביעית. The small amounts matter only for someone who shows that he values them by putting them away. That person is liable even for the small amount.

keyTerms.meaning: Measures, meaning the minimum amounts.
Those who store them away, which shows they consider the amount valuable.

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion in the משנה (the תנא קמא) gives each liquid its own amount. רבי שמעון says a רביעית for everyone, unless the person himself stores the smaller amounts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: all of them are a quarter-log,
and all these measures were not stated
except for those who store them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion inside the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All liquids are measured by a רביעית. The smaller amounts apply only to a person who stores them.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds that the wine amount is for a nice cup
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that sharpens the משנה: the wine amount is enough to mix a 'nice cup'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: enough to mix a nice cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that adds one word to the משנה's wine rule. That word is 'nice'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said 'a cup'. The ברייתא says the cup must be a nice, proper one. This tells us the amount is measured by a cup that has some importance, not just any small cup.

keyTerms.meaning: A nice, proper cup.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
enough to mix a nice cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the wine amount in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine amount is what is needed to mix a nice cup.

steps.title: What counts as a nice cup?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means by a 'nice cup'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the phrase 'nice cup'. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Nice' is a vague word. The גמרא wants a clear, defined kind of cup so that the amount can actually be measured.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is...?

phrases.english: And what is a nice cup —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא's term means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is a כוס יפה?

steps.title: A nice cup is a cup of blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a 'nice cup' is a כוס של ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: a 'nice cup' means the cup used for a ברכה, such as for ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוס של ברכה has set, known rules. So the vague 'nice cup' is now tied to a cup with a defined size.

keyTerms.meaning: A cup of blessing, the wine cup used for a ברכה such as ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: A cup of blessing.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כוס יפה is a כוס של ברכה.

steps.title: How much wine a cup of blessing needs
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says a כוס של ברכה needs a quarter of a רביעית of strong wine. When it is diluted, it fills a full רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: a cup of blessing must contain a quarter of a רביעית of wine, so that one can dilute it and it will come up to a full רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the actual size of a כוס של ברכה. This tells us the amount of wine for carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strong wine was mixed with about three parts water to one part wine. A quarter of a רביעית of wine plus the water therefore makes a full רביעית to drink. So the carrying amount for wine is a quarter of a רביעית of strong wine.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a quarter-log.
And it will come up to (a certain amount).

steps.whatToRemember: Wine for carrying: a quarter of a רביעית of strong wine. That is the amount that becomes a full רביעית כוס של ברכה after mixing with water.
steps.whyThisMatters: This also teaches a practical rule for any כוס של ברכה: it must end up holding at least a רביעית.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
A cup of blessing needs
to have in it a quarter of a quarter-log,
so that he can dilute it
and it will come up to a quarter-log.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the size of the כוס של ברכה identified in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כוס של ברכה needs a quarter of a רביעית of strong wine, which becomes a רביעית after dilution.

steps.title: רבא begins to bring support
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens with 'we too...', starting a support for רב נחמן's ruling. The statement continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to say that we can also learn this rule from another source. This is only the opening words. The rest comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אף אנן נמי' usually introduces a proof that we already know this rule from a משנה. Here it backs up the size of a כוס של ברכה. The actual source has not appeared yet.

keyTerms.meaning: We too also (have learned this). It opens a supporting proof.

phrases.english: Rava said: we too also
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a support for רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a כוס של ברכה needs a quarter of a רביעית of wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Not yet quoted. It continues on the next amud.
